title: Checks for statements which have no effect.
summary: Unlike dead code, these statements are actually executed. However, as they have no effect, all they do is make the code less readable. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for replace statements which have no effect.
summary: It’s either a mistake or confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for binding to underscore prefixed variable without side-effects.
summary: Unlike dead code, these bindings are actually executed. However, as they have no effect and shouldn’t be used further on, all they do is make the code less readable. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for Rust ABI functions with the #[no_mangle] attribute.
summary: The Rust ABI is not stable, but in many simple cases matches enough with the C ABI that it is possible to forget to add extern "C" to a function called from C. Changes to the Rust ABI can break this at any point. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for non-ASCII characters in string and char literals.
summary: Yeah, we know, the 90’s called and wanted their charset back. Even so, there still are editors and other programs out there that don’t work well with Unicode. So if the code is meant to be used internationally, on multiple operating systems, or has other portability requirements, activating this lint could be useful. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for non-canonical implementations of Clone when Copy is already implemented.
summary: If both Clone and Copy are implemented, they must agree. This can done by dereferencing self in Clone’s implementation, which will avoid any possibility of the implementations becoming out of sync. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for non-canonical implementations of PartialOrd when Ord is already implemented.
summary: If both PartialOrd and Ord are implemented, they must agree. This is commonly done by wrapping the result of cmp in Some for partial_cmp. Not doing this may silently introduce an error upon refactoring. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for any and all combinators in cfg with only one condition.
summary: If there is only one condition, no need to wrap it into any or all combinators. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for non-octal values used to set Unix file permissions.
summary: They will be converted into octal, creating potentially unintended file permissions. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: This lint warns about a Send implementation for a type that contains fields that are not safe to be sent across threads.
summary: It tries to detect fields that can cause a soundness issue when sent to another thread (e.g., Rc) while allowing !Send fields that are expected to exist in a Send type, such as raw pointers. Sending the struct to another thread effectively sends all of its fields, and the fields that do not implement Send can lead to soundness bugs such as data races when accessed in a thread that is different from the thread that created it. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Lints when once_cell::sync::Lazy or lazy_static! are used to define a static variable, and suggests replacing such cases with std::sync::LazyLock instead.
summary: Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for conversions from NonZero types to regular integer types, and suggests using NonZero types for the target as well.
summary: Converting from NonZero types to regular integer types and then back to NonZero types is less efficient and loses the type-safety guarantees provided by NonZero types. Using NonZero types consistently can lead to more optimized code and prevent certain classes of errors related to zero values. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for boolean expressions that can be written more concisely.
summary: Readability of boolean expressions suffers from unnecessary duplication. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for unsafe usage of NonNull::new_unchecked(Box::into_raw(x)), and suggests calling NonNull::from_mut(Box::leak(x)) instead.
summary: NonNull::new_unchecked is an unsafe function, which we don’t need to call at all if we can instead use a mutable reference. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for duplicate open options as well as combinations that make no sense.
summary: In the best case, the code will be harder to read than necessary. I don’t know the worst case. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks that common macros are used with consistent bracing.
summary: Having non-conventional braces on well-stablished macros can be confusing when debugging, and they bring incosistencies with the rest of the ecosystem. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for public functions that dereference raw pointer arguments but are not marked unsafe.
summary: The function should almost definitely be marked unsafe, since for an arbitrary raw pointer, there is no way of telling for sure if it is valid. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.
